findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 58 of 58 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 4 of 26 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the bus itself can take them.

findings.effort: A small file for most flat-fare systems.
findings.fix: Add fare_attributes.txt (or Fares v2 files) with your fare structure. If your service is fare-free, ask to have it marked fare-free instead.
findings.what: The feed contains no fare information.
findings.why: Riders see 'fare unknown' in trip planners and can't budget their trip; visitors are most affected.

findings.effort: Usually one value per route pattern in your scheduling source.
findings.fix: Add the destination, direction, or 'via' label riders actually see to trip_headsign. Do not copy the route name. If the label changes during the trip, use stop_headsign.
findings.what: 4 of 26 trips lack rider-facing destination or direction text.
findings.why: When a route has multiple directions or patterns, the route name alone may not tell riders which service is coming.

findings.what: feed_info.txt has no technical contact (feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url).
findings.why: Trip-planning apps and regional data coordinators have nobody to email when they spot a problem with your feed, so problems linger.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 0% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (0% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is not published.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'missing_timepoint_value' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Missing timepoint value (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A review pass in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Remove retired stops from the export, or add them back to the trips that should serve them.
findings.what: Some stops exist in the feed but no trip ever stops at them.
findings.why: Riders may walk to a stop where no bus is scheduled to arrive.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged trip.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stop times for transposed minutes.
findings.what: Some scheduled trips move faster between stops than a bus can.
findings.why: Usually a typo'd stop time; riders get arrival times no bus can meet.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'fast_travel_between_far_stops' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Fast travel between far stops (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Usually a re-export from your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Export and publish an updated GTFS feed that covers at least the next 30 days of service.
findings.what: This feed's service calendar runs out within the next 7 days.
findings.why: When the calendar ends, Google Maps and other trip planners drop your agency entirely. Riders see no service at all.

findings.effort: One field, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt lists no contact email and no contact URL.
findings.why: Without a contact, apps like Google Maps can't reach you when they find a problem in the feed.

findings.effort: A field at a time; not urgent.
findings.fix: Review the flagged fields and fill in the ones your riders would use.
findings.what: Some files leave out fields that GTFS asks for but does not require.
findings.why: Recommended fields like agency_phone or stop descriptions make the feed more useful to riders and trip planners.

findings.effort: Usually an export-tool fix, not hand editing.
findings.fix: Re-generate shape_dist_traveled on export so stop and shape distances use the same units.
findings.what: On some trips the stop distances run a little past the end of the route line.
findings.why: The stop and shape distance values don't quite line up, so any math that uses them can drift.

findings.effort: A quick look at the flagged files.
findings.fix: Check the flagged column names for misspellings of standard GTFS fields; remove them if they are vendor extras.
findings.what: Some files contain columns that are not part of the GTFS spec.
findings.why: Harmless to riders, but apps ignore these columns and they can hide typos in real column names.

findings.effort: Two fields in feed_info.txt, or one export setting.
findings.fix: Widen feed_start_date and feed_end_date to cover all service dates, or fix the dates that fall outside.
findings.what: Some service dates fall outside the date window set in feed_info.txt.
findings.why: feed_info.txt should span every day your service runs, so apps know when the data applies.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'feed_valid_beyond_total_service_window' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Feed valid beyond total service window (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Usually one export setting; export on a schedule so it never lapses again.
findings.fix: Re-export the feed with a calendar that reaches further out, and set feed_info feed_end_date past your next service change.
findings.why: When the calendar runs out, trip planners stop showing this agency even though the buses are still running. Riders are told the service does not exist.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 1 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (2).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 7 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("Rt 205/Rt 11 - Hartwick", "Dollar General/NBT Bank - Richfield Springs", "Chestnut Street/Oneida Street - Oneonta", and more).
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.

findings.effort: A cleanup pass in your scheduling software.

findings.why: Riders see these stops in apps and on the map but can never catch anything there, which erodes trust in the data.
